one_line: React hooks expose shared, stateful tools across existing editors and work queues.
what_it_does: Adds WebMCP tool registration to React applications and demonstrates human-agent collaboration across Handoff, calendar, Excalidraw, and Puck tabs.
leverage_rationale: The central value is structured, live in-tab state shared by people and multiple agents across editors; coordinate-level UI automation would be markedly less reliable and cannot reproduce the same semantic handoff cleanly.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes person, browser agent, and coding agent claiming, declining, and editing the same work in one tab.
Transcript describes item claims, tool switching, typed tool calls, shared queue return, and destructive-action confirmation.
React hook lifecycle and per-editor tool registries are part of the demonstrated product.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually coherent end-to-end evidence spanning library API, shared queue, four editor integrations, and a live demo, with some visual evidence unavailable to this review.
execution_evidence: Facts report live demo, public repository, nine gallery images, and a 115-second video.
Transcript describes complete launch workflow through board, calendar, diagram, and landing-page tools.
Publish remains human-only and confirmation boundaries are explicitly described.
impact_rationale: A reusable integration layer that makes established React tools agent-operable addresses a broad developer and end-user collaboration problem with credible practical value.
impact_evidence: The project targets open-source tools people already use rather than a toy standalone app.
It ships a hook-based integration model and live landing page explaining the library.
The workflow returns outputs to a human-review queue.
creativity_rationale: The combination of a React-native tool-registration library with a shared launch room and cross-editor handoff is a fresh, ambitious use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Four distinct editors are coordinated through one shared work queue.
The concept treats WebMCP as an integration surface for existing software, not merely a button wrapper.
usability_note: The described queue, confirmations, and semantic tools suggest strong usability; visual verification was unavailable.
red_flags: Image inspection was blocked by vision-tool rate limiting, so visual claims are not independently checked.
standouts: Strong shared-state and multi-editor WebMCP thesis.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with coherent cross-application workflow and credible execution evidence.

one_line: Bilingual privacy-first discovery of safe wellbeing exercises and human support.
what_it_does: Lets people or browser agents filter and read psychoeducational exercises and find general support options without diagnosis or personal data.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools can safely expose bounded wellbeing content and urgency-aware support lookup, though a general agent could achieve much of the read/filter outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Four named WebMCP tools expose exercise and support capabilities.
The product emphasizes privacy, safety boundaries, and no diagnosis.
The ordinary interface already supports the core browsing task.
execution_rationale: The scope is clear and the packet reports a live demo, but there is no submitted video and limited end-to-end evidence.
execution_evidence: Facts report live demo, public repo, and four gallery images.
Description specifies bilingual views, filters, complete instructions, and safety notes.
impact_rationale: People seeking low-intensity, stigma-reducing psychoeducational support are a real audience, and bilingual privacy-preserving access is a credible fit.
impact_evidence: English-Spanish support is explicit.
The product addresses uncertainty and stigma around seeking help.
Safety and emergency limitations are included.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful health-safety framing and bilingual agent access provide a real angle, but the underlying exercise-discovery concept is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Privacy-first, non-diagnostic boundary is central.
Human-support options are paired with agent-discoverable exercises.
usability_note: Clear filters and safety notes suggest accessible use; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No video and thin packet evidence cap execution confidence.
Health content requires careful safety validation not demonstrated here.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
standouts: Keeps diagnosis and emergency claims out of scope.
advance_reason: Meaningful social value, but leverage and execution evidence are not strong enough for advancement.

one_line: A human-controlled family admin queue turns scattered obligations into reviewed next steps.
what_it_does: Unifies fictional school, calendar, home, and notes actions; agents filter, explain, and prepare drafts while parents approve visibly.
leverage_rationale: Structured action state, provenance, confidence, and draft preparation make agent assistance safer and more repeatable than UI driving, but the workflow remains largely achievable with general automation.
leverage_evidence: Tools filter by area, owner, status, and deadline.
Agent can explain source, confidence, requirements, and next step.
Final approval, submission, and removal remain human-controlled.
execution_rationale: The prototype has a coherent narrow scope and explicit controls, but only five deterministic fictional actions and no video limit demonstrated completeness.
execution_evidence: Description states five deterministic fictional actions.
Audit history and visible final buttons are described.
Live demo is reported but public repository is absent.
impact_rationale: Household coordination is a real recurring burden for parents and the human-control model directly addresses trust concerns.
impact_evidence: Target audience and school/calendar/home use case are specific.
Draft-first workflow preserves parent final say.
creativity_rationale: The calm unified household queue and provenance-aware assistant are a useful synthesis, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Unmatched local captures become distinct actions.
Source and confidence are first-class action properties.
usability_note: Calm queue and review controls sound usable; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: Fictional deterministic data and no video limit proof of real-world robustness.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
advance_reason: Good practical concept but evidence and ambition appear mid-band.

one_line: Procurement agents shortlist suppliers and prepare purchases under human approval.
what_it_does: Searches and ranks marketplace offers, compares suppliers, requests simulated quotes, drafts purchases, and tracks orders.
leverage_rationale: Procurement is multi-step and constraint-heavy; typed marketplace state and explicit confirmation materially improve reliability over UI navigation.
leverage_evidence: Structured ranking includes verification, fit, availability, budget, warranty, delivery, and rating.
Tools cover search, comparison, quote, draft, confirmation, and tracking.
confirm_purchase returns HUMAN_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED until visible approval.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and well-bounded, with a live demo and public repo, but no video or gallery evidence limits certainty about completion.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.
Description covers the end-to-end procurement lifecycle.
Simulated marketplace and quote behavior are explicit.
impact_rationale: Small-business owners have a concrete time-consuming procurement problem and the proposed workflow directly reduces comparison and preparation work.
impact_evidence: Specific laptop-under-budget example.
Supplier trust, warranty, delivery, and order status are addressed.
creativity_rationale: Human-gated procurement with structured supplier reasoning is a fresh, ambitious application of WebMCP, though procurement automation is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Combines ranked constraints, quote requests, drafts, and approval in one agent surface.
Website remains marketplace source of truth.
usability_note: Goal-oriented request and explicit purchase gate are strong usability choices; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No video or gallery images; simulated data may understate operational complexity.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
advance_reason: Strong practical impact and major WebMCP delta with a coherent human-in-the-loop workflow.

one_line: A local-first canvas editor lets agents perform precise image annotations alongside people.
what_it_does: Edits local images with text, shapes, blur, arrows, drawings, crops, styling, positioning, and export through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Stable object IDs, image-local coordinates, and shared editor actions make precise canvas editing substantially more reliable than generic browser automation.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP tools connect directly to shared Fabric.js editor actions.
The project identifies responsive coordinate consistency as a core challenge.
Description claims a complete upload-to-export agent workflow.
execution_rationale: The feature set and implementation choices are coherent, but evidence is a single description with no video and limited packaging.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported.
React, TypeScript, Fabric.js, and Vite stack is specified.
Blur synchronization and coordinate handling are acknowledged.
impact_rationale: Designers and users doing repetitive precise annotations are a clear audience, and local-first editing provides credible privacy value.
impact_evidence: Use cases include blur, arrows, crops, and repeated annotation.
Future face detection is framed as local-first.
creativity_rationale: Agent-controlled visual editing with coordinate-aware object operations is a strong medium fit and more than a generic image generator.
creativity_evidence: Complete editing workflow in one interaction is claimed.
Stable IDs and explicit coordinate system are deliberate interaction design.
usability_note: Direct canvas collaboration is promising; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No video and only one gallery image.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and concept, but execution evidence is too thin for advancement.

one_line: A guided grant-appeal workspace finds overlooked evidence while keeping submission human-controlled.
what_it_does: Shows rejection reasons, deadlines, rules, records, and appeal forms; agents locate relevant evidence and prepare previews before human submission.
leverage_rationale: Case-linked records, decision rules, evidence sufficiency, and receipts are structured semantics that general UI agents could easily misapply; WebMCP materially improves correctness.
leverage_evidence: Agent finds an uploaded attendance record and connects it to the decision factor.
A weak second case is blocked because records do not prove the required sessions.
Submission requires explicit applicant confirmation and returns a receipt.
execution_rationale: The two-case design demonstrates both successful and blocked paths and describes a coherent end-to-end workflow, though no video is supplied.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repo, and four gallery images are reported.
Success and insufficiency cases are both specified.
Receipt and next review step complete the happy path.
impact_rationale: People facing opaque grant rejections have a specific high-stakes problem; surfacing rules and overlooked valid evidence can provide substantial practical benefit.
impact_evidence: Decision factors, deadline, evidence rules, and records are consolidated.
The Maya Chen case demonstrates a plausible overlooked-record problem.
Human control is retained for submission.
creativity_rationale: Evidence sufficiency and appeal preparation form a memorable, socially useful application with a deliberately demonstrated failure mode.
creativity_evidence: The product distinguishes overlooked evidence from evidence that does not prove the claim.
Blocked appeal preview is an important trust-oriented interaction.
usability_note: One-page case context and explicit missing-evidence explanation support usability; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No video; execution claims rely on text and packaging.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
standouts: Demonstrates both positive and safety-blocked paths.
advance_reason: High credible impact and strong semantic WebMCP leverage in a carefully bounded workflow.

one_line: Humans and agents negotiate meeting times together, with visible voting and human lock-in.
what_it_does: Runs live scheduling sessions where participants vote, counter-propose, rank slots, and converge while an audit log records human and agent actions.
leverage_rationale: The live shared negotiation state and agent participation as an equal, logged actor are central; generic UI driving is brittle for this stateful multi-party protocol.
leverage_evidence: Seven page-registered tools read state, join, vote with reasons, counter-propose, and rank.
Every action lands in a shared HUMAN or AGENT negotiation log.
Only the human organizer can accept or lock the final time.
execution_rationale: The protocol is unusually well specified and includes a claimed first-try chained agent test, but no video reduces observed completion confidence.
execution_evidence: Live demo, five gallery images, and no public repo are reported.
Description covers candidate times, votes, counter-proposals, convergence, and lock-in.
Testing claim describes a four-tool chain from read state to winner report.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across constrained participants is a common real problem, and agent negotiation can reduce poll friction while preserving organizer authority.
impact_evidence: Specific yes/maybe/no and counter-proposal workflow.
Mixed human-agent participation addresses coordination overhead directly.
creativity_rationale: Treating scheduling as a live negotiation in which human and agent participants vote and counter-propose is a genuinely memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agents are equal participants rather than hidden assistants.
Shared audit log makes the negotiation legible.
usability_note: Visible proposals, reasons, and logs support trust; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No public repo or video; claimed testing is not independently observed.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and standout interaction model outweigh limited execution evidence.

one_line: A person and an agent edit the same design canvas using live selection state.
what_it_does: Forks a browser design editor so agents generate, translate, align, recolor, and modify selected objects in the shared canvas.
leverage_rationale: Access to actual selected objects in live in-memory document state is the product's core capability and cannot be reproduced comparably by scraping coordinates or generic agents.
leverage_evidence: Agent reads the actual objects selected by the person.
WebMCP runs against the application's JavaScript object graph and live canvas.
Description contrasts this with brittle coordinates, accessibility scraping, and extensions.
execution_rationale: The concept and claimed editor workflow are coherent, with public repo and live demo, but no video limits end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Facts report public repository, live demo, and three gallery images.
Description covers real-time design, selection-aware edits, and variant production.
The forked editor provides a concrete host application.
impact_rationale: Designers face repetitive localization, alignment, and brand-variant work; selection-aware agent assistance addresses that specific burden without replacing creative control.
impact_evidence: Examples include multilingual headlines, grid alignment, recoloring, and platform versions.
Human can point at objects rather than name layers.
creativity_rationale: The interaction of pointing/selecting on a canvas while an agent operates on the exact live selection is highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Actual cursor selection is surfaced semantically to the agent.
Design object graph and human-agent co-editing are treated as one shared medium.
usability_note: Point-and-say interaction is compelling; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No video; execution evidence is claimed rather than observed.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
standouts: Selection-aware collaboration is a strong WebMCP thesis.
Clear designer pain point and interaction model.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and highly original canvas interaction make this a strong advance despite limited packet verification.

one_line: A local ancient-DNA workbench turns cohort definitions and visual findings into shared research objects.
what_it_does: Filters a large ancient-DNA dataset, saves named cohorts, compares populations, finds neighbors/outliers, attaches findings, and exports reports through linked visual panels and WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The agent and researcher share a rich, visual, stateful scientific workspace where named cohorts and PCA/map/timeline context matter; generic UI automation would be unreliable and lose semantic provenance.
leverage_evidence: 22,202 individuals and 276,725 SNPs are represented in one workspace.
Named cohorts, comparisons, neighbors, outliers, findings, and journal are shared objects.
Three linked visual panels plus table and research state are exposed to the agent.
execution_rationale: The packet describes an unusually complete research workbench and real dataset with many linked surfaces, though the absence of video limits direct proof.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repo, and four gallery images are reported.
Dataset provenance, version, compatibility, SNP count, and license are specified.
Export paths include data, workspace, and Markdown research report.
impact_rationale: Researchers in ancient DNA and adjacent fields have a concrete reproducibility and exploration problem, and named cohort objects can replace fragile one-off scripts.
impact_evidence: Specific methods sentence and R-script pain point motivate the product.
Research workflow connects filtering, visual discovery, interpretation, and reporting.
Open CC0 source dataset is identified.
creativity_rationale: The concept turns implicit cohort definitions and visual discoveries into collaborative, agent-revisable scientific objects, an ambitious and memorable research interaction.
creativity_evidence: PCA outliers can lead to agent-assisted identity and publication exploration.
Map, two PCA bases, timeline, table, cohorts, and journal share one state.
usability_note: Rich linked panels could be powerful but potentially dense; visual verification unavailable.
red_flags: No video; scientific correctness and performance are not independently verified.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
standouts: Exceptional domain specificity and research impact.
Makes cohort definitions first-class, revisable objects.
advance_reason: High leverage, impact, and creativity with a deeply coherent research workflow.

one_line: A governed knowledge workspace controls what future agents may rely on.
what_it_does: Collects bounded evidence, runs deterministic checks, supports human approval and lineage, and exposes only current in-scope admitted knowledge to successor agents.
leverage_rationale: Structured governance state, evidence lineage, scope, freshness, and authority boundaries are materially safer and more precise through page-native tools than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Tools cover workspace summary, review queue, evidence, lineage, checks, policy, and agent access.
Agents cannot approve knowledge, reveal secrets, activate policy, or issue credentials.
Human owner approval is a hard gate for admission.
execution_rationale: The governance model is coherent and ambitious, but the demo is reported dead and no video exists, sharply limiting execution-claimed confidence.
execution_evidence: Facts report public demo link as dead, no video, and six gallery images.
Description specifies proposal, deterministic checks, optional LM advice, approval, retrieval, and append-only activity.
End-to-end workflow is described but not shown live.
impact_rationale: Teams deploying agent-produced decisions and research need provenance, freshness, scope, and human authorization; this addresses a real emerging governance gap.
impact_evidence: The product targets a concrete question: what may the next agent safely rely on.
Lineage and append-only activity preserve proposal, evaluation, and authorization history.
Successor retrieval is constrained to admitted current knowledge.
creativity_rationale: An agent-produced knowledge management and admission-control layer is a distinctive response to a fast-growing problem, with unusually explicit authority design.
creativity_evidence: Optional LM judge is advisory rather than authoritative.
Knowledge admission is separated from generation and automated checks.
usability_note: Governance surfaces may be valuable but likely complex; live usability cannot be checked because demo is dead.
red_flags: Demo link is reported dead.
No video and no public execution proof.
Image inspection blocked by vision-tool rate limiting.
advance_reason: High impact and good leverage, but dead demo and absent video make execution too uncertain.
